title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A · Paper 1F — original full-length mock
subject: pearson-igcse-mathematics-a
subjectLabel: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
instructions: Answer all 22 questions. The total time is 2 hours; there is no separate reading period. Write your answer and all working in each question's response area; add pages if needed. A permitted scientific calculator may be used. The Formula reference attached to every question contains the tier-specific supplied formula facts. Draw your own labelled diagrams or graphs where requested; all necessary coordinates and measurements are provided. Do not infer measurements from a sketch. Use a suitable scale and label axes. Give units where appropriate. Keep unrounded working; give non-exact final numerical answers to 3 significant figures unless otherwise stated. This is an original DigitalDP practice paper, not a Pearson paper. Digital drawing is a classroom adaptation, not a test of physical ruler-and-compass accuracy.

resources.label: Foundation formula reference
resources.text:
Formula reference — independently typeset mathematical facts
Trapezium: area = ½(a + b)h, where a and b are parallel side lengths and h is perpendicular height.
Prism: volume = cross-sectional area × length.
Cylinder: volume = πr²h; curved surface area = 2πrh. Here r is radius and h is perpendicular height.

questions.label: Question 1 — Number skills
questions.prompt: (a) Write 6047 in words. [1] (b) Calculate 38 × 24. [1] (c) Put −2, 0.7, −0.5, 0 in ascending order. [1] (d) Round 7.846 to 2 decimal places. [1]

questions.label: Question 2 — Fractions
questions.prompt: (a) Write 18/24 in simplest form. [1] (b) Calculate 5/6 − 1/4. [2] (c) Find 3/5 of 140. [1]

questions.label: Question 3 — Shopping
questions.prompt: A notebook costs $2.35 and a pen costs $1.60. (a) Find the cost of 4 notebooks and 3 pens. [2] (b) A customer pays with $20. Find the change. [1] (c) Pens are also sold in packs of 5 for $7.25. Find the saving per pen compared with buying one pen. [1]

questions.label: Question 4 — Algebra expressions
questions.prompt: (a) Simplify 5a + 3b − 2a + b. [1] (b) Expand 4(2x − 3). [1] (c) Factorise 6y + 15. [1] (d) Find 2p² − q when p = −3 and q = 5. [1]

questions.label: Question 5 — Powers and factors
questions.prompt: (a) Express 84 as a product of prime factors. [2] (b) Find the highest common factor of 84 and 126. [1] (c) Calculate √169 + 2³. [1]

questions.label: Question 6 — Number patterns
questions.prompt: A sequence begins 7, 11, 15, 19. (a) Write the next two terms. [1] (b) Write an expression for the nth term. [2] (c) Is 103 a term? Explain using your expression. [2]

questions.label: Question 7 — Equations and inequality
questions.prompt: (a) Solve 5x − 7 = 28. [2] (b) Solve 3(y + 2) = 24. [2] (c) List all integer values of n satisfying −2 < n ≤ 2. [1]

questions.label: Question 8 — Standard form and estimates
questions.prompt: (a) Write 0.00072 in standard form. [1] (b) Write 3.5 × 10⁵ as an ordinary number. [1] (c) Calculate (6 × 10⁴) ÷ (2.5 × 10²), giving standard form. [2] (d) Estimate 19.8 × 5.1 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure. [1]

questions.label: Question 9 — Angles
questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle BAC = 44°. (a) Find angle ABC, giving a reason. [2] (b) BC is extended beyond C to D. Find angle ACD. [1] (c) A regular polygon has exterior angle 30°. Find its number of sides and one interior angle. [2]

questions.label: Question 10 — Garden plan
questions.prompt: A rectangular garden is 12 m by 8 m. A rectangular pond 3 m by 2 m lies completely inside it. (a) Find the garden's perimeter. [1] (b) Find the remaining area. [2] (c) Grass seed covers 15 m² per bag. Find the smallest number of bags needed for the remaining area. [2]

questions.label: Question 11 — Transformation
questions.prompt: Triangle T has vertices A(1,1), B(4,1), C(1,3). (a) Draw T on coordinate axes. [1] (b) Reflect T in the y-axis and state all image coordinates. [2] (c) Instead translate the original T by the column vector (−2, 3). State the image of A and explain whether its area changes. [2]

questions.label: Question 12 — Averages
questions.prompt: Six scores are 4, 7, 7, 8, 9, 13. (a) Find the mode. [1] (b) Find the median. [1] (c) Find the mean. [1]

questions.label: Question 13 — Probability
questions.prompt: A bag holds 5 red, 3 blue and 2 white counters. One is selected at random. (a) Find P(blue). [1] (b) Find P(not white). [1] (c) Over 200 selections with replacement, estimate the number of red selections. [1]

questions.label: Question 14 — Frequency chart
questions.prompt: Twenty-four students choose one activity: art 6, chess 8, music 4, sport 6. (a) Draw a labelled bar chart. [2] (b) Calculate the angle for chess in a pie chart. [2]

questions.label: Question 15 — Recipe and scale
questions.prompt: Flour, oats and seeds are mixed in the ratio 5:3:2. A batch contains 360 g of oats. (a) Find the total mass of the batch. [2] (b) Find the mass of seeds. [1] (c) A new batch has total mass 1.8 kg. Find the extra flour needed compared with the first batch. [2]

questions.label: Question 16 — Ticket equations
questions.prompt: A museum charges one price for an adult ticket and one price for a child ticket. Two adult tickets and three child tickets cost $39. Three adult tickets and two child tickets cost $46. (a) Form two equations. [2] (b) Find each ticket price. [3]

questions.label: Question 17 — Quadratic model
questions.prompt: A rectangle has width x cm and length (x + 5) cm. Its area is 84 cm². (a) Form an equation in x. [1] (b) Solve your equation and explain which solution is possible. [3] (c) Find the perimeter. [1]

questions.label: Question 18 — Coordinate graph
questions.prompt: The line L has equation y = 3x − 4. (a) Complete a table for x = −1, 0, 1, 2. [2] (b) Plot these points and draw L on labelled axes. [2] (c) State the gradient of L. [1]

questions.label: Question 19 — Percentage comparison
questions.prompt: A bicycle marked at $480 is reduced by 15%. (a) Calculate the sale price. [2] (b) A different shop sells the same bicycle for $420. Find the percentage by which its price exceeds the sale price. [3]

questions.label: Question 20 — Ramp geometry
questions.prompt: A straight ramp rises 0.9 m over a horizontal distance of 4.8 m. (a) Find its sloping length. [3] (b) Find its angle to the horizontal, to 1 decimal place. [2]

questions.label: Question 21 — Cylinder container
questions.prompt: An open-top cylindrical container has internal radius 4 cm and height 12 cm. Ignore thickness. (a) Calculate its capacity in millilitres. [2] (b) Find the area of material forming its curved wall and single circular base. [3]

questions.label: Question 22 — Grouped travel times
questions.prompt: Travel times t minutes for 30 students are grouped as follows: 0 < t ≤ 10: 4; 10 < t ≤ 20: 12; 20 < t ≤ 30: 9; 30 < t ≤ 40: 5. (a) State the modal class. [1] (b) Estimate the mean time. [3] (c) Explain why the exact mean cannot be found from these data. [1]
